# TDPdf v1.18.0.0

A fork-sync release pulling the newest useful features and fixes from upstream [**SteveTheKiller/KillerPDF**](https://github.com/SteveTheKiller/KillerPDF) (v1.6.3 and v1.6.4) and adapting them to TDPdf's diverged multi-tab architecture. This build ships everything merged to `main` since the last release, headlined by the changes below. See [`CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/doodlemania2/TDPdf/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) for the complete per-version history.

As always: this fork only exists because upstream KillerPDF is a genuinely great, dark-themed, no-telemetry, no-cloud Windows PDF editor. **Go star [the upstream project](https://github.com/SteveTheKiller/KillerPDF).**

## Highlights

### Edit bookmarks right in the sidebar (new in 1.18.0.0)
The Outline panel is now a full bookmark editor. Add a bookmark (a **"+ Add bookmark"** row you name in place), rename inline (**F2**), add child bookmarks, reorder, retarget to the current page, delete, and delete-all — with Ctrl/Shift multi-select and a right-click menu. Every edit is a single **Ctrl+Z**. Read-only files show the outline without editing.

### A command line (new in 1.18.0.0)
`TDPdf.exe` now runs headlessly with real exit codes — and works while the app is open:

```
TDPdf.exe --merge a.pdf b.pdf -o out.pdf
TDPdf.exe --split in.pdf --pages 1-3,7 -o out/
TDPdf.exe --to-image in.pdf --dpi 200 --format png -o out/
TDPdf.exe --flatten in.pdf -o flat.pdf
TDPdf.exe --ocr scan.pdf --lang eng -o searchable.pdf
TDPdf.exe --decrypt locked.pdf --password secret -o open.pdf
TDPdf.exe --help
```

Each command reuses the exact pipeline the app itself runs, so the output matches what you'd get from the GUI. A launch with no command still just opens the file in the app.

### A visual keyboard map (new in 1.18.0.0)
The shortcuts overlay (**F1** / **Ctrl+?**) gains a **LIST / KEYBOARD** toggle. In keyboard mode, a rendered keyboard lights every bound key, color-coded by category; hold **Ctrl / Shift / Alt** (or click a layer) to preview that layer, and hover a key to see what it does. Follows the active theme, and remembers your choice.

### Big documents stay light on memory (1.18.0.0)
Continuous view used to keep a rendered image of **every** page for the life of the document — a long, image-heavy PDF could balloon to gigabytes. It now keeps images only for the pages around what you're looking at, rendering pages as they come into view and releasing those that leave. Closing a tab now actually returns that memory.

### More navigation, the way the big viewers do it (1.18.0.0)
- **Jump history:** **Alt+←** / **Alt+→** (and the mouse back / forward buttons) retrace bookmark, link, jump-box, and Home/End jumps, browser-style.
- **Home / End** go to the first / last page.
- **Ctrl+1 / Ctrl+2 / Ctrl+3** = actual size / fit width / fit page.
- **Two-Page mode** now turns a full spread at a time.
- **Menu key / Shift+F10** opens the right-click menu from the keyboard.

## Fixes
- **No more save corruption.** Saving now cleans three problems that made strict viewers (and Adobe) reject files, and re-saving *heals* files already damaged by other tools: a dangling empty bookmark reference, a zero-size crop box ("page dimensions out-of-range"), and a stale digital-signature value that a re-save invalidates.
- **Fixed an intermittent crash** while scrolling or clicking through annotation-heavy pages.
- **Fixed a crash** opening a PDF whose page tree has zero pages.
- **Chinese (and other) bookmark titles** no longer show as garbled text in password-protected PDFs.
- **Grid → Continuous** no longer clips zoomed pages, and the page counter now tracks scrolling in Grid view.
- **Re-saving no longer reduces PDF/A conformance** — the PDF engine is now vendored so conformance bugs are fixed at the source (no metadata stamping on open, correct stream lengths, spec-correct booleans, and no stray transparency groups).

## Install / update
Download `TDPdf-v1.18.0.0-win-x64.exe` below — a single self-contained Windows x64 executable, no install required. Run it from anywhere, or let it offer to install per-user on first launch. Existing installations update in place.
